pr.title: Let scoped sessions write reactions and bookmarks on listed channels
pr.description:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
#### Summary
Stacked on #39368 (which stacks on #39367). Review those first; this diff only adds the write grant.

Scoped sessions from #39367 are read-only. This adds a small, generic write grant so a plugin can let a scoped bot session react to posts and manage bookmarks in a short list of channels, while keeping every other write denied. Nothing here is specific to any plugin feature.

**Model (`server/public/model`)**
- `SessionScope.WritePermissions []string` (`write_permissions`): a subset of the new `model.ScopeWritePermissions`: `add_reaction`, `add_bookmark_{public,private}_channel`, `edit_bookmark_{public,private}_channel`, `order_bookmark_{public,private}_channel`.
- `SessionScopeResources.WriteChannelIDs []string` (`write_channel_ids`): at most `model.SessionScopeMaxWriteChannelIDs` (5), each also in `ChannelIDs` (so never a DM or GM, which `CreateScopedSession` already rejects).
- `IsValid` requires write permissions and write channels to come together, and the scope to hold `read_channel_content`. Write permissions in `Permissions` are still rejected.
- Helpers: `IsSessionScopeWritePermission`, `HasWritePermission`, `ListsWriteChannel`, `GrantsWrites`.
- Both fields are `omitempty`, so read-only scopes serialize exactly as before.

**Enforcement (`EvaluateSessionScope`)**
- A write permission is allowed only if all of these hold:
  - the scope grants it
  - the target resolves to a channel in `WriteChannelIDs`
  - the scope can read that channel (not archived, not policy-enforced, not a DM or GM)
  - the bot holds the permission there without the scope (normal RBAC plus channel access enforcement)
- So the grant only narrows the bot's own permissions and never adds to any. Team-wide and system-wide checks for these permissions are always denied.
- Read checks now also require the permission to be in `ScopeReadPermissions`. That way a tampered stored scope that lists `create_post` in `Permissions` fails closed.

**Routes**
- New `scopedSessionWrite` handler flag. It admits a scoped session only when its scope grants writes, and the handler's own permission checks then decide each write.
- Flagged write routes: `POST /reactions`, `POST /channels/{id}/bookmarks`, `PATCH /channels/{id}/bookmarks/{id}`, and `POST /channels/{id}/bookmarks/{id}/sort_order`.
- `GET /channels/{id}/bookmarks` gets the read flag.
- `POST /posts`, deleting reactions or bookmarks, and every other write route stay denied.
- On write routes, a scoped session gets the scope error for every refusal. For example, writing to an archived channel no longer returns a distinct "archived" error that would reveal the channel exists.

**Exact channel lists:** a scope with only `ChannelIDs` (no `OpenTeamPublicChannels` and no `PublicChannelTeamIDs`) already reads exactly those channels. The new tests pin this down for an open team: other public channels, member channels, the team channel list and post search all stay limited to the listed c
